$comment: GitHub label manifest. Source of truth for product repositories.
Labels are not files in the repository - they are a GitHub-side setting.
Applied by: node tools/sync-github.mjs --labels | bash
The whole manifest is in pure ASCII - names AND descriptions. A label is an identifier
used in scripts, filters and URLs, and mangled characters in a URL are a source of silent mistakes.
Descriptions are ASCII because the path manifest -> node -> PowerShell -> gh has places where
Windows PowerShell 5.1 re-encodes text via the console code page and corrupts national characters.
Instead of configuring encodings along the way, the manifest simply has nothing to corrupt.
The generator is meant to check this - a character outside ASCII stops the run.
The same manifest applies across all product repositories. A label meaning
something different in two repositories is worse than two different labels.
Substitute your own state/role names for the keys below - the structure (states/roles/decisions/gaps/severity)
is what should stay, the content of each label is an example to adapt.

states.$comment: The story's state machine. Exactly one state label per Issue.

labels.name: state:analysis
labels.description: Analyst establishes acceptance criteria and the Definition of Done row

labels.name: state:design
labels.description: Architect builds an impact map for architectural decisions

labels.name: state:decision
labels.description: GATE 1 - waiting on a human decision: scope and architecture

labels.name: state:implementation
labels.description: Developer writes the schema change (if applicable), code and tests

labels.name: state:qa
labels.description: QA writes negative and contrast tests, runs mutations

labels.name: state:merge
labels.description: GATE 2 - waiting on a human decision: review and merge the PR

labels.name: state:closed
labels.description: Evidence provided, status raised

roles.$comment: Who currently holds the ball. The role label says who is working, the state says at which stage.

labels.name: role:po
labels.description: Product Owner - scope and business justification

labels.name: role:analyst
labels.description: Analyst - acceptance criteria

labels.name: role:architect
labels.description: Architect - impact map for architectural decisions

labels.name: role:backend
labels.description: Backend developer

labels.name: role:frontend
labels.description: Frontend developer

labels.name: role:qa
labels.description: QA - negative, contrast tests, mutations

labels.name: role:invariant-guardian
labels.description: Invariant Guardian - diff audit

$comment: Labels that stop work. 'waiting-on-human' is the most important in the whole
set: one filter showing everything that is standing and waiting for you, regardless
of stage. Without it you'd have to remember which states are gates.

labels.name: waiting-on-human
labels.description: Standing and waiting for a decision - one filter for all gates

labels.name: adr-deviation
labels.description: Requires a new architectural decision or an explicit deviation from an existing one

labels.name: blocked
labels.description: Cannot move without an external resolution

labels.name: evidence:missing
labels.description: Code exists, evidence doesn't - the task cannot be checked off

$comment: Work ordered by the other repository. The Issue is created WHERE the work
needs to be done - the frontend finds a gap in the backend, so the Issue is created in <repo-backend>.
Full rules: process/cross-repo-gaps.md.
'gap:awaiting-contract' has its own name because this is the state in which such reports
most often die quietly: the reporter proposed a shape, the recipient hasn't responded,
and both sides think the ball is with the other one.

labels.name: gap:reported-by-frontend
labels.description: Work in this repository ordered by the frontend repository

labels.name: gap:reported-by-backend
labels.description: Work in this repository ordered by the backend repository

labels.name: gap:awaiting-contract
labels.description: Contract shape proposed by the reporter, recipient has not yet responded

severity.$comment: Severity of an Invariant Guardian report. Scale from agents/invariant-guardian.md - adapt to your own list of invariants.

labels.name: severity:high
labels.description: Data leak between clients, incorrect billing, silent data loss, a security mechanism that appears to work but doesn't

labels.name: severity:medium
labels.description: API contract, missing evidence, a defect under concurrency or retry

labels.name: severity:low
labels.description: Documentation drift, language, convention with no functional effect
